data.name: Agnethe
data.gender_notes: Agnethe is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Latin Agnus, meaning ‘lamb’. This name was borne by several early Christian saints, including St. Agnes of Rome. In Christian tradition, Agnes was a virgin martyr who, though offered to the god of fertility, remained devoted to her faith and was eventually executed. The name Agnethe carries the meaning “Lamb, Agnes” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Agnethe usually hope their child will grow to embody lamb, agnes and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Agnethe belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lamb, Agnes.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Agnethe total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Αγνή
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἡ Αγνή ἐίναι ὄνομα Χριστιανικό, ἀπὸ τὴν Ἑλληνικὴ γλῶσσα, καὶ σημαίνει ἁγνή, ἀγαθή, καὶ εὐσεβής, προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὸ Ἑλληνικὸ ῥῆμα ἀγνός, τὸ ὁποῖο σημαίνει καθαρότητα καὶ ἁγνότητα, καὶ ἐνδιαφέρει στὴν Χριστιανικὴ παράδοση

in_latin.name: Agnetis
in_latin.long_meaning: Agnetis est nomen Christianum, ex lingua Graeca, et significat sanctam, puram, et benevolam, derivatum est a verbo Graeco ἀγνή, quod significat puritatem et sanctitatem, et interest in traditione Christiana

in_english.name: Agnethe
in_english.long_meaning: Agnethe is a Christian name derived from the Greek word hagnē, meaning pure and chaste, and is associated with the virtues of purity and kindness, and is significant in Christian tradition as a symbol of moral integrity

data.cultural_impact: Agnes was considered a defender of virginity and purity. She embraced her martyrdom at a young age, which has made her a symbol of courage in the face of adversity and an inspiration for subsequent generations.
data.spiritual_significance: Agnes is a reminder of the power and importance of faith, even in the most difficult of circumstances. Her unwavering devotion to God, despite the allure of worldly pleasures and the threat of death, serves as a testament to the deeper truths that lie within the human soul.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Agnethe is a variant of Agnes, derived from the Latin word hagnos, meaning pure or chaste. Named after the early Christian martyr St. Agnes, Agnethe represents virginity, purity, and deep devotion to God. The name evokes a sense of sacredness, innocence, and strength, reminding us of the virtues to be found in the heart of a faithful Christian.
